title: Rxjs — Module Quiz
description: Mixed quiz covering all topics in Rxjs.

questions.question: A key difference: a Promise emits ___ value(s); an Observable emits ___ value(s).
questions.explanation: A Promise settles once with a single value; an Observable is a stream that can emit 0..n values then complete/error.

questions.question: Observables are lazy. What does that mean?

options.text: They do nothing until you subscribe()

questions.explanation: Creation functions (of, from, http.get) set up a blueprint; side effects/execution start only on subscribe.

questions.question: How do you cancel an in-flight Observable (e.g. an HTTP request)?
questions.explanation: Calling subscription.unsubscribe() tears down the stream; Angular's async pipe does this automatically.

questions.question: Which operator turns an array into an Observable that emits each item?
questions.explanation: from() iterates an array/iterable/promise and emits each element; of() emits the arguments as discrete values.

questions.question: Promise.all vs forkJoin (RxJS) — key difference?

options.text: forkJoin emits only after ALL input observables complete; Promise.all after all resolve

questions.explanation: forkJoin waits for completion of each source (HTTP calls complete) then emits the last value of each — like Promise.all.

questions.question: What does the async pipe do in Angular templates?

options.text: Converts a Promise to an Observable
Subscribes, renders the latest value, and auto-unsubscribes on destroy
Runs code in a Web Worker

questions.explanation: The async pipe unwraps Observables/Promises and handles subscription lifecycle — preventing memory leaks.

questions.question: A component is fundamentally a...?

options.text: A class decorated with @Component that controls a view template

questions.explanation: Components pair a TS class with a template + metadata via @Component to render a UI region.

questions.question: Which decorator metadata defines the HTML tag name?
questions.explanation: selector defines the custom element name (e.g. 'app-root') used in templates.

questions.question: What is the default change detection strategy that checks every component on each event?
questions.explanation: Default strategy runs change detection on every tick; OnPush restricts it to input/event/observable changes.

questions.question: Which lifecycle hook runs ONCE after the first render, when inputs are bound?
questions.explanation: ngOnInit is called once after the first ngOnChanges, once component inputs are available.

questions.question: To communicate parent -> child, you use...?
questions.explanation: @Input() properties receive data from a parent component's template binding.

questions.question: Standalone components (Angular 15+) do NOT require...?
questions.explanation: Standalone components declare their own imports and can be used without being declared in an NgModule.

questions.question: What decorator marks a class as available to the DI system as a singleton service?
questions.explanation: @Injectable() marks a class as a service that the injector can create and provide.

questions.question: What is the hierarchical injector tree in Angular?

options.text: Root, module, and component-level injectors that resolve tokens up the tree

questions.explanation: Angular has a tree of injectors; a component gets the nearest provider, walking up to root if absent.

questions.question: Providing a service in a component's `providers` array means...?

options.text: A new instance is created per component instance
It becomes a singleton for the whole app
Only the module can use it

questions.explanation: Component-level providers create a new instance scoped to that component (and its children), not app-wide.

questions.question: What is the `providedIn: 'root'` alternative to?

options.text: Listing the service in a module's providers array

questions.explanation: providedIn:'root' registers the service with the root injector without manually adding it to providers.

questions.question: What is the `inject()` function used for?

options.text: Injecting dependencies inside injection contexts (e.g. field initializers)

questions.explanation: inject() is a standalone alternative to constructor injection, usable in fields, factories, and in routes/guards.

questions.question: How does Angular know WHICH dependency to inject by type?

options.text: It guesses from the variable name
From the constructor parameter type + emitted decorator metadata

questions.explanation: DI resolves tokens via constructor param types, using design:paramtypes metadata when available.

questions.question: What does Zone.js do for Angular change detection?

options.text: Patches async APIs so Angular knows when to run a CD cycle

questions.explanation: Zone.js notifies Angular after async operations (events, timers, XHR) so a CD pass runs.

questions.question: OnPush components re-check ONLY when...?

options.text: An @Input reference changes, an event originates from the component, or an observed Observable emits

questions.explanation: OnPush skips a component unless its inputs change by reference, it emits an event, or async pipe notifies.

questions.question: Which method manually triggers change detection on a component/view?
questions.explanation: ChangeDetectorRef.detectChanges() runs CD for the current view immediately.

questions.question: markForCheck() vs detectChanges()?

options.text: markForCheck flags the view to be checked in the NEXT cycle; detectChanges runs it now
Both only work in OnPush off

questions.explanation: markForCheck() marks the component and ancestors dirty; detectChanges() actually runs CD synchronously.

questions.question: Why is mutating an array in place (push) problematic with OnPush?

options.text: The reference is unchanged, so OnPush may skip re-rendering

questions.explanation: OnPush compares input references; in-place mutation keeps the same reference, so the view may not update.

questions.question: What is `NgZone.runOutsideAngular()` used for?

options.text: To run code WITHOUT triggering Angular CD (e.g. third-party libs / RAF loops)

questions.explanation: Running outside the zone avoids unnecessary CD cycles for frequent updates you control manually.

questions.question: Which statement best describes the purpose of "Rxjs"?

options.text: It is a focused area of frontend knowledge with its own set of patterns and trade-offs.
It is only useful for legacy codebases.
It cannot be tested in isolation.
It is deprecated in modern browsers.

questions.explanation: "Rxjs" groups related concepts, APIs, and best practices you should be able to reason about and apply.

questions.question: When working inside "01-rxjs", the most effective way to retain the material is to:

options.text: Read the core principles, implement sample code, and test understanding via quizzes.

questions.explanation: Active recall combined with hands-on practice leads to mastery.
